stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether guided hints help children learn to solve puzzles. They recruited 64 five-year-old children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition solved practice puzzles with hints from an adult that were gradually reduced. Children in the other condition solved the same practice puzzles alone. The researchers then recorded the number of new puzzles out of ten that each child later solved without help.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.
Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.
Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They hypothesized that whether a small request came first would affect compliance with a large request.

**Participants.** The sample was 120 homeowners, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

**Results.** The group that was first asked to sign the petition: agreed to display the sign (%) = 55. The group that was only asked to display the sign: agreed to display the sign (%) = 18. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 80 students were randomly assigned to be alone or with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants who were alone reported the smoke after a mean of 58 seconds; those in groups took a mean of 196 seconds (p = 0.01), and many never reported it.

**Source B.** In interviews after a staged emergency, participants who had not helped often said that they 'assumed someone else had already called for help' or that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

**Source C.** Researchers observed 300 staged incidents in which a person dropped a bag of shopping in the street. Help was offered in 82 percent of incidents on quiet streets and in 41 percent of incidents on crowded streets.

questions.stem: When a dog lunges at him, Evan's heart pounds and his muscles tense, ready for him to run or defend himself. Which response to stress is this?

options.why: Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.
Correct. The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.
Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.
Distress is the negative stress that harms well-being and performance.

questions.explanation: The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.

questions.stem: Which gland releases hormones that direct the other endocrine glands?

options.why: Correct. The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.
The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.

questions.explanation: The pituitary gland is the master gland of the endocrine system, which is controlled by the hypothalamus.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Debriefing happens after the study.
Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 9, 7, 11, 13, 22, 9, 6. What is the median of the scores?

options.why: Correct. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven.
That is the mean.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 6, 7, 9, 9, 11, 13, 22. Put the scores in order and take the middle one, the fourth of seven. The one very high score pulls the mean (11) above the median (9), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them?

options.why: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.
Correct. A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.
Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Obedience is the following of the direct commands of an authority figure.

questions.explanation: A superordinate goal is a shared goal that can be reached only if groups cooperate, which reduces conflict between them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes semantics?

options.text: The whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate
options.why: That describes grammar.

options.text: The smallest unit of language that carries meaning
options.why: That describes a morpheme.

options.text: The rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences
options.why: Correct. This is what semantics means.

options.text: The smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language
options.why: That describes a phoneme.

questions.explanation: Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.

questions.stem: To treat severe epilepsy, surgeons cut the fibers that carry messages between the left and right hemispheres. Which structure was cut?

options.why: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
Correct. The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.stem: A client afraid of dogs learns to relax, then stays relaxed while imagining a dog, seeing a photo, and finally patting a dog. Which treatment is this?

options.why: A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.
Correct. Systematic desensitization is the exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli.

questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization is the exposure therapy that pairs relaxation with a graded series of anxiety-arousing stimuli.

questions.stem: A man is certain that government agents have planted a transmitter in his tooth, and no evidence can change his mind. Which symptom is this?

options.why: A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.
Correct. A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.explanation: A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.65. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Replication is repeating a study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The caffeine group was tested in the morning, and the decaffeinated group was tested late at night
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: One group differed from the other in caffeine
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: The two groups differed in attention at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Taking a tablet makes Lena's headache go away, so she is more likely to take a tablet next time. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.
Consent is obtained before the study.
A placebo is an inactive treatment.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: A researcher tests the same 200 children every two years from age 6 to age 30. Which research design is this?

options.why: Correct. A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.
Stability and change is the developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter.
Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.
A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.

questions.explanation: A longitudinal study is research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period.

questions.stem: A logo is made of three separate curved lines, but people see a complete circle. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Correct. Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: When a toy is hidden under a blanket, a five-month-old acts as if it has vanished, but a ten-month-old lifts the blanket to find it. What has the older infant developed?

options.why: Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.
Correct. Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.
Egocentrism is the difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view.
Theory of mind is the understanding that other people have their own thoughts, beliefs and feelings.

questions.explanation: Object permanence is the understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.55. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance?

options.why: Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.
Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Correct. Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.
Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.

questions.explanation: Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.

questions.stem: A charity first asks people to sign a petition and a week later asks the same people for a donation. Which technique is this?

options.why: The central route to persuasion is persuasion that works through evidence and logical arguments, which people think about carefully.
Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.
The halo effect is the tendency for one good quality of a person to make us assume they have other good qualities.
Correct. The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.explanation: The foot-in-the-door technique is the strategy of getting agreement to a small request first so that a larger request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: A researcher sends a questionnaire about sleep habits to 2,000 adults. Which research method is this?

options.why: An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.
Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
Correct. A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.
An operational definition is a statement of exactly how a variable is measured or manipulated in a study.

questions.explanation: A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes executive functions?

options.text: The mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what executive functions means.

options.text: The inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose
options.why: That describes functional fixedness.

options.text: A step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution
options.why: That describes an algorithm.

options.text: Thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem
options.why: That describes divergent thinking.

questions.explanation: Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.

questions.stem: At a normal weight, Tara secretly eats huge amounts of food and then makes herself vomit. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Correct. Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.
A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.explanation: Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.

questions.stem: Without considering any alternatives, Ravi plans to join the family business because his parents always expected it. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Correct. Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.explanation: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.stem: Too little of the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter is linked to seizures, tremors and insomnia. Which neurotransmitter is this?

options.why: Correct. GABA is the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter.
Endorphins is the neurotransmitters that reduce pain and increase pleasure.
Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that influences movement, attention, and feelings of reward.
Serotonin is the neurotransmitter that affects mood, hunger and sleep.

questions.explanation: GABA is the brain's main inhibitory neurotransmitter.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes shape constancy?

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes
options.why: Correct. This is what shape constancy means.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes
options.why: That describes size constancy.

options.text: The perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting
options.why: That describes color constancy.

options.text: The perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession
options.why: That describes apparent movement.

questions.explanation: Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: While studying, Vera notices that she does not really understand one section and decides to change her study method. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Recall is the retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question.
Correct. Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.
Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.
Recognition is the identification of previously learned information when it is presented, as in a multiple-choice question.

questions.explanation: Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the Flynn effect?

options.text: Originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100
options.why: That describes the intelligence quotient.

options.text: The theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal
options.why: That describes multiple intelligences.

options.text: The single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks
options.why: That describes general intelligence.

options.text: The steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations
options.why: Correct. This is what the Flynn effect means.

questions.explanation: The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: That would show a positive correlation.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate negative correlation appears as a band of points sloping downward.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

questions.explanation: A moderate negative correlation appears as a band of points sloping downward.

questions.stem: After brain surgery, a patient remembers his past but forgets each new person minutes after meeting them. Which condition does he have?

options.why: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Correct. Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.explanation: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder?

options.why: An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
Correct. Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.explanation: Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.stem: A dog's salivation to a tone has died away. The next day, the tone is sounded and the dog salivates again. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Acquisition is in classical conditioning, the first stage, in which the neutral stimulus is paired with the unconditioned stimulus and the response is learned.
Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.
Correct. Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.why: Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Omar generally feels that he is a valuable and likeable person. Which term describes this overall feeling?

options.why: Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.
Self-concept is all the thoughts and feelings a person has in answer to the question 'Who am I?'.
Correct. Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.explanation: Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes long-term memory?

options.text: The relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences
options.why: Correct. This is what long-term memory means.

options.text: The brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second
options.why: That describes iconic memory.

options.text: The memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten
options.why: That describes short-term memory.

options.text: The active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory
options.why: That describes working memory.

questions.explanation: Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.stem: Positive psychologists group gratitude, hope, humor and spirituality under which virtue?

options.why: Temperance is the category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control.
Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Correct. Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.
Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.

questions.explanation: Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the autonomic nervous system?

options.text: The sensory and motor nerves that connect the brain and spinal cord to the rest of the body
options.why: That describes the peripheral nervous system.

options.text: The division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body for fight or flight
options.why: That describes the sympathetic nervous system.

options.text: The division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort
options.why: Correct. This is what the autonomic nervous system means.

options.text: The division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body and conserves energy
options.why: That describes the parasympathetic nervous system.

questions.explanation: The autonomic nervous system is the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls glands and internal organs without conscious effort.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: A man with strong aggressive urges becomes a successful boxer. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Correct. Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes social anxiety disorder?

options.text: The disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations
options.why: Correct. This is what social anxiety disorder means.

options.text: The culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly in Japan, marked by fear of offending or embarrassing others
options.why: That describes taijin kyofusho.

options.text: The disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months
options.why: That describes generalized anxiety disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain
options.why: That describes panic disorder.

questions.explanation: Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.

questions.stem: The group that held the pen between the teeth rated the cartoons as funnier. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen and amusement are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The facial expression produced by holding a pen caused the difference in amusement
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: An American psychiatrist checks a patient's symptoms against the criteria in the standard manual published by the American Psychiatric Association. Which manual is this?

options.why: Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.
Deviation from the social norm is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects.
Correct. The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.

questions.explanation: The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: Because his neighbor looked after his cat last month, Abe feels he should help the neighbor move house. Which norm is guiding him?

options.why: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
An industrial-organizational psychologist is a psychologist who studies behavior in the workplace to improve productivity and well-being.
Correct. The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.explanation: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.stem: Leah paints every evening simply because she loves doing it. Which kind of motivation is this?

options.why: Correct. Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.

questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.

questions.stem: After the election result is announced, Tom says, 'I knew all along that she would win,' although he had predicted the opposite. Which bias is this?

options.why: Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Correct. Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.explanation: Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.stem: A researcher reports that two variables are related, with r = +0.62. What is this number called?

options.why: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
The third variable problem is the possibility that an unmeasured factor causes the relationship between two correlated variables.
Correct. The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.
The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.

questions.explanation: The correlation coefficient is the number from −1.00 to +1.00 that shows the direction and strength of a relationship.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it?

options.why: A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.
Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.
Correct. Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.

questions.explanation: Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.

questions.stem: After being rejected by a university, Hal says, 'I never really wanted to go there anyway; it is too far away.' Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Correct. Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.
Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.

questions.explanation: Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.stem: A therapist does not give advice; she listens with empathy and accepts whatever her client says, trusting the client to find his own answers. Which therapy is this?

options.why: Hypnosis is a state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories.
Correct. Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.
Free association is the psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind.
Active listening is the technique of echoing, restating and seeking clarification of what the client says.

questions.explanation: Person-centered therapy is the humanistic therapy in which the therapist provides acceptance and empathy so that the client can grow.

questions.stem: After a coin lands heads five times in a row, Rita is sure the next toss must be tails. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.
Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.
The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.
Correct. The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.explanation: The gambler's fallacy is the mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.28, −0.93, −0.44, +0.61. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.28 is closer to zero.
+0.61 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.93 is farthest from zero.
−0.44 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.93 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron carries the action potential away from the cell body?

options.why: Correct. The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.
The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.

questions.explanation: The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes aphasia?

options.text: The arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body
options.why: That describes contralateral control.

options.text: An impairment of language caused by brain damage
options.why: Correct. This is what aphasia means.

options.text: The area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production
options.why: That describes Broca's area.

options.text: The area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension
options.why: That describes Wernicke's area.

questions.explanation: Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies?

options.why: Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Correct. Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.

questions.explanation: Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: A 3D film sends a slightly different image to each eye, and the brain uses the difference to perceive depth. Which depth cue is this?

options.why: Texture gradient is the monocular depth cue in which surfaces look smoother and less detailed as they get farther away.
Relative size is the monocular depth cue in which the object that casts the smaller image is seen as farther away.
Relative clarity is the monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones.
Correct. Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.

questions.explanation: Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.

questions.stem: Harlow's infant monkeys spent most of their time clinging to a soft cloth 'mother' rather than a wire one that gave milk. This finding shows the importance of which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.
Separation anxiety is the distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months.
Anxious attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child is very upset by separation and is not easily comforted on reunion.
Avoidant attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child seems indifferent when the caregiver leaves and ignores the caregiver on return.

questions.explanation: Contact comfort is the comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned?

options.why: Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Correct. Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.explanation: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.stem: For a week, a patient sleeps two hours a night, speaks rapidly, starts ten projects and feels invincible. Which state is this?

options.why: Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Correct. Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.

questions.explanation: Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

options.text: The number of other people present
options.why: This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.
A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which structure changes its curvature, in a process called accommodation, to focus near or far objects?

options.why: The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.
Correct. The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.
Cones is the receptor cells that detect color and fine detail and work in bright light.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.

questions.explanation: The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.

questions.stem: Troubled by constant thoughts of germs, Dee washes her hands forty times a day. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.
Correct. Obsessive-compulsive disorder is the disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions.
An obsession is an unwanted thought or urge that keeps returning and causes anxiety.
Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.explanation: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is the disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions.

questions.stem: A driver cuts in front of Ruth, and she immediately concludes he is a rude person, never considering that he may be rushing to a hospital. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The actor-observer bias is the tendency to explain our own behavior by the situation but other people's behavior by their traits.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
Correct. The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.stem: After a study in which participants were misled about its purpose, the researcher explains what was really being studied. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.
Correct. Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.
Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.

questions.explanation: Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: In a drug trial, half of the patients receive no active medication so that their results can be compared with the others. This half is which of the following?

options.why: The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.
A placebo is an inactive substance or treatment that looks like the real one.
Correct. The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.
Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.

questions.explanation: The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.

questions.stem: At six months, a baby says 'da-da-da' and 'ma-ma-ma' without meaning anything by it. Which stage of language development is this?

options.why: Correct. Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.
Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.explanation: Babbling is the stage from about four months in which infants produce many consonant-vowel sounds, such as 'ba-ba'.

questions.stem: After a railway accident damaged the front of his brain, Phineas Gage became impulsive and unable to plan. Which lobes were damaged?

options.why: The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.
The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
Correct. The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a case study?

options.text: A recording of the electrical waves that sweep across the brain's surface
options.why: That describes an EEG.

options.text: An in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage
options.why: Correct. This is what a case study means.

options.text: The brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience
options.why: That describes neuroplasticity.

options.text: The destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function
options.why: That describes lesioning.

questions.explanation: A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the evolutionary perspective?

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

options.text: The study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself
options.why: That describes epigenetics.

options.text: The influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes
options.why: That describes nature.

options.text: The approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce
options.why: Correct. This is what the evolutionary perspective means.

questions.explanation: The evolutionary perspective is the approach that explains behavior through natural selection of traits that helped ancestors survive and reproduce.

questions.stem: Between ages 11 and 14, Dev grows quickly and his body becomes capable of reproduction. Which period is this?

options.why: Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Correct. Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.explanation: Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of compliance with a large request

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of compliance with a large request.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Compliance with a large request was defined as the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. On average, the value was 55 for the group that was first asked to sign the petition and 18 for the group that was only asked to display the sign, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 120 homeowners from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. (55 compared with 18).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that whether a small request came first affects compliance with a large request. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to whether a small request came first. The finding illustrates the foot-in-the-door technique: agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a larger one, partly to stay consistent and avoid cognitive dissonance.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: People are less likely to help when others are present, because each person feels less responsible and looks to others to decide how to act.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, participants who were alone reported smoke after 58 seconds, but those in groups of five took 196 seconds.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: when others are present, each person feels less personal responsibility to act.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants said that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through informational social influence: in an unclear situation, people use the behavior of others as evidence of what is happening, so if nobody reacts, each person concludes there is no emergency.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
